name: BYTE PHANTOM
realCapabilities: CAMERA PRIVACY AUDIT: Windows read-only inspection of current-user camera consent, desktop-app consent, LetAppsAccessCamera device policy and recorded per-app webcam access entries/timestamps; Android checks only BYTE PHANTOM's own declared CAMERA permission, current permission grant and AppOps mode. No camera device is enumerated or opened, no frames are captured, and no camera permission is added.

FIREWALL INTELLIGENCE: Windows reads the effective Windows Defender Firewall ActiveStore profiles, service state, default inbound/outbound actions, enabled-rule direction/action counts and up to 120 enabled rule summaries. Read-only; no rules are modified and no elevation prompt or network probe is requested.

CREDENTIAL LAB: cross-platform local password generation using Web Crypto getRandomValues, unbiased rejection-sampled character selection, configurable 12–64 character length and four selectable character groups; generated secrets are excluded from reports, activity history and local storage, and copied only on explicit user action

FILE INTEGRITY: Windows open-file dialog and Android Storage Access Framework picker; streaming SHA-256 calculation, optional reference-digest comparison, byte count and metadata-only stability check; no file upload or file modification

PROCESS INTELLIGENCE: Windows read-only top-80 process inventory with PID, working-set memory, CPU time, start time and accessible executable path; Android current BYTE PHANTOM app-process PSS/heap and device memory only

Captive Portal and HTTPS Response Integrity checks: strict per-provider HTTP status and expected body validation for Microsoft NCSI, Google connectivity, Cloudflare connectivity, and Apple captive portal probes
HTTPS checks do not follow redirects; report redirect destination host, response byte count, expected status, body match, and response-integrity state
Android native ConnectivityManager captive-portal, validated-network, and internet-capability indicators when available
OUTAGE WATCH stores captive-portal assessment, redirect counts, and unexpected HTTPS response counts with CSV/JSON export
Network Shutdown Intelligence: cross-platform route/DNS/upstream/endpoint isolation using three independent system DNS names and four HTTPS providers
Per-destination reachability matrix identifies partial connectivity and endpoint-specific failures instead of treating one reachable test host as proof of full internet access
OUTAGE WATCH stores successful DNS and HTTPS target counts for each sample and exports the counts to CSV/JSON
OUTAGE WATCH issue confirmation: two consecutive qualifying failures before opening an incident and two consecutive successful HTTPS checks before recovery
OUTAGE WATCH DNS, HTTPS, and gateway response latency history with a recent trend view and rolling median baselines
Cross-platform OUTAGE WATCH: interval-based gateway/DNS/HTTPS connectivity checks, local incident start/recovery timeline, and JSON/CSV export
Cross-platform private IPv4 Network Radar and persistent local journal
Interactive observed LAN map
Read-only gateway, DNS resolver, transport, interface, local IPv4, and default-route intelligence on Windows and Android
Layered connectivity diagnosis: active route snapshot, one local gateway ICMP echo, system DNS resolution, and two independent HTTPS/TLS checks on Windows and Android
DNS resolver intelligence: direct UDP/53 DNS A-query tests for configured IPv4 DNS servers and Cloudflare, Google Public DNS, and Quad9 reference resolvers
DNS answer comparison for example.com and iana.org across configured IPv4 DNS servers and Cloudflare, Google Public DNS, and Quad9
Non-public DNS answer review flags and peer-majority divergence indicators, with explicit CDN/GeoDNS caveats

Per-name answer consistency, sample response rate, median latency, latency range and median absolute deviation jitter metrics

Local history captures sample success rate, number of repeat-stable resolvers, best resolver median latency and jitter; visual trend covers latest eight tests

Local backup of the original Windows DNS mode (automatic/DHCP or static) and original IPv4 DNS server list before applying an override

connectivityDiagnostics.gatewayProbe: One ICMP echo request to the active private IPv4 default gateway, when reported and supported
checks: one ICMP echo to the active private IPv4 gateway when reported and supported
system DNS resolution for example.com, iana.org, and cloudflare.com
HTTPS/TLS GET checks against Microsoft, Google, Cloudflare, and Apple test services
connectivityDiagnostics.interpretation: HTTPS success requires both an expected HTTP status and the provider's expected body signature; redirects are not followed. A redirect, HTTP 511, or repeated unexpected content can indicate a captive portal or interception but is not a malware verdict. Android also reports native OS captive-portal and validated-network flags when available. A missing gateway ICMP response remains inconclusive. No probe proves unrestricted access to the entire internet.

captivePortalDetection.android: ConnectivityManager NET_CAPABILITY_CAPTIVE_PORTAL, NET_CAPABILITY_VALIDATED, and NET_CAPABILITY_INTERNET when available
responseSignals: multiple independent 2xx responses with unexpected body signatures
captivePortalDetection.confidence: A single unexpected response is a warning, not conclusive proof. These probes cannot identify all transparent proxies or TLS interception.

security: Connectivity diagnostics run only after an explicit user action or while the operator has started OUTAGE WATCH with NETWORK RADAR open. They read the active route, send one ICMP echo to the active private IPv4 gateway when available, perform three system DNS lookups, and make four fixed HTTPS GET checks. HTTPS requests do not follow redirects and only retain a bounded response sample for expected-signature validation; response bodies are not stored in history or exported. Android reads ConnectivityManager captive portal, validated, and internet capability flags when available. The app does not scan LAN hosts or ports, test credentials, exploit devices, or modify network settings. DNS intelligence sends direct DNS A queries only to configured IPv4 DNS servers and fixed public resolver references. DNS answer divergence and non-public address flags are advisory indicators only, not a malware verdict. Windows DNS changes remain opt-in, limited to the active default-route adapter, require UAC Administrator approval, and preserve a local original-configuration backup. Android opens system network settings for manual changes only. FILE INTEGRITY reads only one explicitly user-selected file using the Windows open-file dialog or Android Storage Access Framework. SHA-256 is streamed in memory; no file content is uploaded, changed or stored by the app. Android document providers may be cloud-backed and can fetch content on the user's behalf. PROCESS INTELLIGENCE is read-only: Windows returns up to 80 processes from Get-Process without elevation; Android reports only the current BYTE PHANTOM app process and device memory, not other apps. CREDENTIAL LAB generates passwords locally with Web Crypto getRandomValues and unbiased selection. The secret is kept only in the current UI memory, is not added to local storage, activity history or reports, and is copied only after explicit user action. No password is sent to any account, authentication endpoint or remote service. FIREWALL INTELLIGENCE reads Windows Defender Firewall ActiveStore profiles and enabled rule summaries using PowerShell NetSecurity read commands. It does not modify firewall rules, profiles or services, does not request UAC elevation, and performs no network probes. Android explicitly reports that the public app API does not expose a global firewall rule inventory; VPN, DNS and connectivity signals are not treated as firewall state. CAMERA PRIVACY AUDIT reads Windows camera consent/policy registry values and recorded per-app access timestamps without opening a camera. On Android it inspects only BYTE PHANTOM's own requested CAMERA permission, current grant and AppOps mode; it does not enumerate other apps or query camera hardware. No CAMERA permission is declared or requested by the audit, no camera stream or frames are opened/captured, and no system settings are modified. Opening privacy settings is an explicit user action. Windows registry timestamps are historical records and do not prove live camera use.

dnsResolverIntelligence.configuredResolvers: Active interface DNS server list from Windows Get-NetIPConfiguration or Android ConnectivityManager/LinkProperties
dnsResolverIntelligence.comparison: Sorts A-record sets for each name and compares responding resolvers. Flags a resolver only when its answer differs from a clear peer majority; non-public answer ranges are separately flagged for review.
dnsResolverIntelligence.recommendation: Fastest resolver with repeat-stable answers for both example.com and iana.org, ranked by mean of per-name medians. Manual IP copy only.
dnsResolverIntelligence.interpretation: Repeat answer variation can occur with DNS load balancing, CDN/GeoDNS, regional routing, split-horizon policy, or transient conditions. It is not proof of poisoning. Three samples provide an operational consistency indicator, not a statistical guarantee.
dnsResolverIntelligence.stabilityRule: A repeat-stable answer requires at least two matching successful A-record sets out of three for each name.

windows.originalDnsModeDetection: Per-adapter Tcpip interface registry NameServer value distinguishes static DNS from automatic/DHCP DNS; effective DNS server list is backed up as well.
windows.apply: Set-DnsClientServerAddress using the selected repeat-stable IPv4 resolver, then read back the active adapter DNS list and verify the requested server.
windows.restore: Restore automatic DNS using ResetServerAddresses or restore the original static server list. Verify mode/list before deleting the local backup.
windows.conflictHandling: If current DNS no longer matches the last app-applied value, stop and request a second explicit confirmation before overwriting it with the original configuration.
windows.uac: Run elevated PowerShell via the native Windows UAC prompt; cancellation is reported without claiming success.

android.action: Open Android wireless/network settings so the user can manually edit the active network DNS.

limitations: Windows applies IPv4 DNS only to the active default-route adapter; other adapters are not modified.
Android ordinary apps cannot directly change device-wide DNS; the user must apply the selected resolver in system settings.
The original Windows backup is local to the app user-data directory. Keep it until the original configuration is restored or manually recorded.

probes: one ICMP echo to the active private IPv4 gateway when available
three system DNS lookups: example.com, iana.org, cloudflare.com
four fixed HTTPS/TLS checks: Microsoft, Google, Cloudflare, Apple

incidentRules.online: At least one fixed HTTPS endpoint returns a successful status
incidentRules.noDefaultRoute: The active operating system route snapshot reports no IPv4 default route
incidentRules.dnsFailure: System DNS lookup fails while the active gateway answered ICMP
incidentRules.httpsUnreachable: System DNS succeeds but both fixed HTTPS test endpoints fail
incidentRules.indeterminate: Remaining mixed or inconclusive probe results; gateway ICMP silence alone is not considered proof of outage

connectivityWatch.lifecycle: Runs only while NETWORK RADAR is open and the app remains active; closing the panel stops the watch. It is not a background system service.

qualityTrend.rollingBaseline: Median of up to the latest 12 successful measurements per metric

classifications: DNS FAILURE (only when all system DNS checks fail and the gateway answered ICMP)
HTTPS UNREACHABLE (DNS succeeds but all HTTPS providers fail)
PARTIAL CONNECTIVITY (at least one HTTPS provider works but one or more tested names or endpoints fail)
ONLINE (all tested names and HTTPS providers respond)

fileIntegrity.windows: Electron open-file dialog; one user-selected regular file is streamed through SHA-256. Before/after size and modification time are compared to flag a file that changed during hashing.
fileIntegrity.android: Android Storage Access Framework ACTION_OPEN_DOCUMENT picker; the selected URI is read through ContentResolver in a streaming SHA-256 pass. No broad storage permission or persistent URI grant is requested.
fileIntegrity.referenceComparison: Optional expected SHA-256 input must be exactly 64 hexadecimal characters. The result reports MATCH, MISMATCH, or NOT REQUESTED.
fileIntegrity.privacy: BYTE PHANTOM does not upload, copy, edit or retain selected file contents. Android document providers may be cloud-backed and can fetch content when the user selects one; this is surfaced in the result.

processIntelligence.windows: PowerShell Get-Process snapshot: total process count and up to 80 processes sorted by working-set memory, including name, PID, memory, CPU time, start time and executable path when access is allowed.
processIntelligence.android: Only the BYTE PHANTOM app's own process PID/UID, PSS and runtime heap plus system available/total memory are reported. Other apps' process details are not enumerated.

credentialLab.generator: Web Crypto getRandomValues with rejection sampling to avoid modulo bias
credentialLab.selection: At least one character from each selected group is guaranteed; remaining characters are sampled from the combined pool and shuffled using cryptographic random integers.
credentialLab.entropyEstimate: Length × log2(unique selected character pool size), displayed as a theoretical pool-based estimate, not a guarantee of real-world password strength.
credentialLab.privacy: Generated secrets exist only in the current renderer memory until the modal closes. They are not written to local storage, activity logs, reports or remote services. Clipboard copy occurs only when explicitly requested.

windows.query: PowerShell NetSecurity Get-NetFirewallProfile and Get-NetFirewallRule using PolicyStore ActiveStore
fields: Windows Defender Firewall MpsSvc service state
Domain / Private / Public profile enabled state
Allow inbound rules / local rule merge / notifications
Up to 120 enabled rule summaries with direction, action, profile and source type

android.explanation: Android public APIs for ordinary applications do not expose a system-wide firewall profile or rule inventory. The app reports this limitation and does not infer firewall state from VPN, DNS, captive portal or network-validation signals.

limitations: Windows firewall state is a read-only snapshot at the time queried; managed policies may change afterward.
Protected or policy-managed rule detail may be incomplete on some Windows installations.
Android global firewall rules cannot be enumerated by this ordinary app.
